faqs.a:
(a)
Dispute of a parking citation.
Notwithstanding any other provision of this Code, a driver or registered owner of
               a vehicle charged with a violation of this division that requires payment for parking
               or involves signage that limits, regulates, restricts, or prohibits the parking, standing,
               or stopping of any vehicle may file a notice of dispute within 15 calendar days from
               the date of service of the citation. Compliance with this time limit shall be a jurisdictional
               prerequisite to any dispute brought under this division. Failure to comply shall bar
               any such dispute.
(b)
Notice of dispute.
The notice of dispute shall be made to the parking enforcement operator who issued
               the citation through the parking enforcement operator's website.
(c)
Appeal of denial of dispute.
a driver or registered owner who is aggrieved by a denial of a dispute by the parking
               enforcement operator may file an appeal within ten calendar days of the date of the
               parking enforcement operator's decision. Compliance with this time limit shall be
               a jurisdictional prerequisite to any appeal brought under this division. Failure to
               comply shall bar any such appeal.
(d)
Notice of appeal.
The notice of the appeal of the parking enforcement operator's decision shall be
               made on a form prescribed by the city and available online on the City of Arvada Website.
               The appeal shall be in writing and shall be filed by electronic means with the public
               works department pursuant to the administrative rules set forth in Article V of Chapter
               2, Division 3 Administrative Hearings, of the Arvada City Code. In such cases where
               good cause is shown, a hard copy of the dispute form may be accepted.
(e)
Review of appeal.
The appeal shall be before a hearing officer appointed by the public works division
               manager or designee thereof. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Code, the
               appeal of a parking citation shall consist of a review of all relevant documentation
               on file with the city in the case, including, but not limited to, the parking citation,
               accompanying documentation, if any, and the appeal form. All documents may be reviewed
               electronically. The city bears the burden of proof in a dispute to establish a parking
               violation by a preponderance of the evidence.
(f)
Decision and enforcement order.
The hearing officer shall issue a written decision and enforcement order within 28
               calendar days of the date of the parking citation. An exception to the date of issuance
               shall be made in any case where, despite due diligence by the city, the city is unable
               to obtain in a timely manner a certified copy of the vehicle registration from the
               division of motor vehicles. In these cases, the decision of the hearing officer shall
               be issued as soon as is reasonably practical after the registration is obtained. Any
               decision shall clearly state whether the driver or registered owner is found responsible
               for the civil parking violation. If the driver or registered owner is found responsible
               for the violation, he or she shall be ordered to pay the civil penalty and any associated
               fees and costs within ten calendar days, unless an appeal to the district court is
               timely filed. The decision shall be dated and shall be served upon the parties pursuant
               to the administrative rules referenced above. Such service may be done electronically.
               A copy of the written decision and enforcement order shall be kept on file in the
               clerk's office in accordance with the city's records retention schedule.
(g)
Final agency decision; appeal.
The decision of the hearing officer shall be a final agency decision. Any final agency
               decision rendered pursuant to this provision may be appealed as set forth in Colorado
               Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 106(a)(4).
(h)
Costs and fees.
The city may assess administrative costs and fees for services required to process
               disputes and appeals of parking citations. Any such costs and fees shall be set pursuant
               to
section 2-261
(a) of this Code.

4561
